personas.name: acute-ischaemia-major-urgent-not-critical
personas.description: An ischaemic ST-depression pattern without ST elevation, ventricular tachycardia, heart block, or a markedly prolonged QTc — severity is graded major (the same severity band as a critical finding), but hasCriticalFinding() is specifically false for isolated ischaemia, so the classification stays 'abnormal' (not 'critical') and follow-up is 'urgent' (within 24 hours) rather than 'critical-alert' (same hour) — a real, non-obvious distinction verified directly against rules.js rather than assumed from the AGENTS.md summary of 'a critical finding'. No originating request reference is linked, so the unexpected-finding flag also fires (ischaemia is one of its three triggers) alongside the abnormal-requiring-action flag.

state.clinicalHistory: Ongoing exertional chest pain, no ST elevation on presentation
state.interpretation: Widespread horizontal ST depression with associated T-wave inversion in the anterolateral leads, consistent with an ischaemic pattern (NSTEMI-type changes). No ST elevation.
state.impression: Ischaemic ECG changes consistent with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Urgent cardiology review within 24 hours; serial troponins
state.clinicianNotes: Originating referral not yet located; patient self-presented to assessment unit

expected.recommendedAction: Arrange urgent clinical review and expedite cardiology referral.
